pr_title: schemachanger: Fix ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN j INT, DROP COLUMN j
pr_body:
Previously, the declarative schema changer errors for ALTER TABLE stmt where we add and then drop the same column. This commit fixes that.

Epic: None
Fixes #110589
Release note: None
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/110851)

> Do we have any guarantees about backwards compatibility of error codes? I can see an argument either way in terms of what code this one should be.

It's a soft guarantee as in customers probably don't expect the error code to change under their feet. What is the old vs the new error code?

@Xiang-Gu ~~what is keeping us from making that error code the same as Postgres?~~

Spoke to @Xiang-Gu offline. I think this change is fine since the error message already doesn't match. And we need this to assert error code when comparatively checking.

@dikshant and I discussed the error code change offline; we agreed that this is okay since they already don't match today.

bors r+

issue_context.title: schemachanger: Error processing ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN k, DROP COLUMN k;
issue_context.body:
```
create table t (i int primary key);
set use_declarative_schema_changer = unsafe_always;
```

We discovered two DDLs that would fail if we force CRDB to use declarative schema changer (by default they are handled by legacy schema changer and they are not implemented). They are
```
alter table t add column j int default 30, drop column j;

ERROR: error executing StatementPhase stage 1 of 1 with 11 MutationType ops: *scop.AddColumnToIndex: &{{{}} 104 3 2 STORED ASC 1 DEFAULT}: column-id "3" does not exist
SQLSTATE: 42703
```
or
```
alter table t add column j int, drop column j;
```
